properties.decision:
Option (a) from req:snapshot-per-revision-not-per-epoch, in a form that keeps existing ids stable. The FIRST capture of a node in an epoch keeps the id `snap:{epoch}:{node}` exactly as before. A genuine SECOND revision in the same epoch appends `:r2`, `:r3`, so HAS_SNAPSHOT becomes one-to-many precisely when history requires it and not before. An IDENTICAL re-capture returns the existing snapshot instead of minting a duplicate — compared against the TAIL of the chain and nothing earlier. A ceiling of 64 distinct snapshots per (epoch, node) errors rather than growing history quietly, and is checked only when a new capture is actually needed, so an idempotent retry against a full chain still succeeds.

NOT chosen: (b) refusing a second record_change in one epoch, and (c) keeping one snapshot per epoch and making the second call a no-op.
properties.name: Snapshot identity is per revision, but only when a revision actually happened
properties.rationale:
Truest to req:intent-preserved, which is the requirement this bug violated — (c) preserves the original but still discards the intermediate, which is losing history on purpose rather than by accident, and (b) pushes epoch hygiene onto the caller when an epoch is meant to bound a round of WORK, not a single edit.

The first-capture id is left unsuffixed because existing graphs and committed exports carry those ids and a test pins one; suffixing everything would have rewritten history to fix a bug about not rewriting history.

Idempotence on an unchanged re-capture is the mirror of the bug being fixed: snapshotting a node that has not moved is a no-op, not a new version, and minting one would make the history claim edits that never happened. It also keeps record_change safe to retry.

TAIL-ONLY COMPARISON, and it is the load-bearing detail. A node edited A -> B -> A inside one epoch has three genuine revisions. Comparing against ANY earlier snapshot would match the first A-capture and hand it back for the third, recording two — hiding an edit that DID happen. That is the same class of loss as the overwrite this fixes, just quieter, and it would have shipped as a half-fix. Matching only the tail also keeps the `:rN` order readable as the order the revisions occurred in, which is the only ordering a reader has: every snapshot in an epoch is pinned to that one epoch and carries no sequence of its own.

The 64 ceiling is a signal, not a storage limit: a node revised that many times inside one epoch means the epoch has stopped bounding anything, and the error says so.

RECORDED AT `proposed`: the requirement itself said the shape of the fix was a choice and none of the options was obviously right. Anthony directed the work be finished, not this particular shape — so the shape is on the record awaiting his word, and reopening it supersedes rather than un-accepts (dec:reopen-supersedes).
